question.text: Per the current NISM II-B workbook (Registration of Nominee section), what is the maximum number of nominees an individual mutual fund investor can appoint per account/folio, and how is the share allocation handled?

answer.text: Up to 10 nominees; if multiple nominees are specified the investor may define percentage shares, otherwise assets are apportioned equally

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current NISM II-B workbook (Registration of Nominee section, p.202), an investor may nominate up to 10 nominees in an account/folio. Page 203 states that where multiple nominees are specified, percentage shares may be defined by the investor; in the absence of specified percentages, assets are apportioned equally among the nominees. The older "maximum 3 nominees" framing on p.165 is no longer the current rule. The Trap: The legacy 3-nominee cap appears in the older portions of the workbook; the current Registration-of-Nominee section explicitly allows up to 10. 1, 2 and 5 are unrelated caps. Cross-Exam Context: NISM V-A and II-B both test the updated 10-nominee rule and the default-equal-apportionment behaviour.
